tytul: Refrigerator cucumber pickle with onion or peppers (Wisconsin Extension)
wstep: This card describes the Wisconsin Extension recipe for cucumber pickles with onions, in which peppers may replace the onion: a refrigerator pickle kept for up to 2 weeks, not canned.

akapity: 8 cups thinly sliced cucumbers and 1 cup sliced onion, or in place of the onion an equal amount of other vegetables such as cauliflower, peppers or carrots.
Pickling solution: 4 cups vinegar (5% acetic acid), 2 cups sugar, 1/3 cup canning and pickling salt, and 1 1/2 teaspoons each of celery seed, mustard seed and turmeric.
Use only vinegar labelled 5% acidity; white and cider vinegar can be used interchangeably; do not use wine vinegars, homemade vinegar or lemon juice.
Vinegar with less than 5% acidity should never be used in home food preservation.
Do not change the proportions of vinegar, vegetables and water in the recipe.
Wash the jars in hot, soapy water, rinse them well and sterilize them by boiling for 10 minutes.
Mix the pickling solution until the sugar dissolves; heating is not required, but it dissolves the sugar and pickles the vegetables faster.
Wash and prepare the vegetables; trim the blossom ends from the cucumbers and discard them.
Fill hot sterilized pint or quart jars with the vegetables, cover them with hot pickling solution and cap the jars with clean lids.
Label and date the jars and store them in the refrigerator at 40 °F (4.4 °C) or colder for up to 2 weeks.
This pickle is not heat processed and must be kept refrigerated.
These pickles are not heat processed, so they are not shelf-stable at room temperature and must be kept in the refrigerator.
Do not decrease the amount of vinegar, because an unsafe product may result; for a milder taste add sugar rather than reduce the vinegar.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep the jar on the middle shelf of the refrigerator, not in the door, because US refrigerator-pickle recipes assume 40 °F (4.4 °C) or colder, while the door can be about 10 °C.
Fresh vegetables are low-acid foods, with a pH above 4.6.
The acid level must be adequate and even throughout the product to prevent the growth of botulism bacteria.
